text_excerpt: St. Annis Hospital has recovered from a devastating ransomware attack that disrupted operations for more than a week last year. The attack, which entered through third-party vendor systems, encrypted critical patient data and forced emergency services to be diverted elsewhere. The hospital administration made the difficult decision not to pay the ransom but instead invested millions of dollars in rebuilding its entire IT infrastructure. New systems include improved network segmentation, mandatory multi-factor authentication, and comprehensive staff training programs. Cybersecurity experts have praised the hospital's transparency in sharing lessons learned from the incident. The total cost of recovery exceeded initial estimates, highlighting the true economic impact of such attacks. Federal regulators have cited this case in discussions about new healthcare security requirements. Despite the painful experience, hospital officials say they are better prepared for future threats. Regional hospitals have formed an information-sharing consortium to distribute threat intelligence and coordinate response to the incident. Tabletop exercises simulating organized attacks now occur quarterly at participating facilities. Cyber insurance premiums have risen sharply, reflecting increased targeting of the healthcare sector by criminal groups. Board-level oversight of cyber risk is now standard practice rather than an exception.
